name: Territorial scope of the polity
framework: Seshat Social Scale (polity territory); Mann 1986 extensive power
anchors: 0 single city-state | 1 multi-city regional state or league | 2 territorial kingdom unifying a region | 3 multi-regional empire with provinces or vassals
proxy: Seshat polity territory (km2); number of cities under one ruler

name: Administrative tiers under royal appointees
anchors: 0 one tier (household or city) | 1 capital + dependent towns | 2 appointed provincial governors | 3 four or more tiers (provinces/satrapies, districts, local) with appointees
proxy: Seshat administrative levels; attested titles of provincial officials

name: Fiscal extraction recorded in writing
framework: Monson and Scheidel 2015; Hanson and Sigman 2021 (extractive capacity); Scott 2017
anchors: 0 none beyond institutional income | 1 ad hoc tribute and gifts | 2 regular levies on land or service, recorded locally | 3 integrated, centrally recorded system across provinces
proxy: named tax or levy systems (bala, gun2 ma-da, ilkum, ginā'u, sāḫu, satrapal taxes) and their archives

name: Royal communication infrastructure
framework: Mann 1984 infrastructural power; Seshat Information (couriers, postal stations)
anchors: 0 none known | 1 ad hoc messengers | 2 regular royal messenger service | 3 relay stations or road network documented by ration records
proxy: messenger texts, road stations, travel rations

name: Weight of the palace (crown) sector
anchors: 0 marginal | 1 present, minor in the record | 2 a major institution | 3 dominant institution of the economy and of the written record
proxy: share of archives from palace or crown households

name: Weight of the temple sector
anchors: 0 marginal | 1 present, minor | 2 major institution | 3 dominant institution of economy and record
proxy: share of archives from temple households

name: Crown control of temples
anchors: 0 autonomous | 1 royal patronage only | 2 royal appointees, levies on temples | 3 temples run as units of the state
proxy: royal officials (qīpu, ša rēš šarri, šabra appointed by king), temple accounts audited by the crown

name: Private (house) sector in writing [reversed in indices]
framework: Diakonoff two-sector model; Van De Mieroop 1992; Garfinkle 2012; Schloen 2001
anchors: 0 negligible | 1 some private legal documents | 2 substantial private archives | 3 private archives dominate the written record
proxy: share of private/family archives (Archibab, Prosobab, CDLI archive field)

name: Standardized administrative procedure
anchors: 0 none detectable | 1 local conventions | 2 standardized accounting within major institutions | 3 standardized procedures across provinces (balanced accounts, instructions for officials, audits)
proxy: balanced accounts, instructions, standardized document types

name: Institutional scribal training
anchors: 0 household apprenticeship, no shared curriculum | 1 shared curriculum, household locus | 2 institutional (palace/temple) schooling with shared curriculum | 3 state-controlled training producing scribes for the whole polity
proxy: find contexts of school tablets; curriculum overlap across cities

name: Codified law and royal justice
framework: Seshat Law (formal legal code, judges, courts); Westbrook 2003; Charpin 2010
anchors: 0 no evidence | 1 royal edicts or royal judgements only | 2 a law collection or royal courts | 3 law collection and royal judges and edicts
proxy: law collections, royal judges (dayyān šarrim), mīšarum edicts

name: State-imposed standards (measures, calendar, dating)
framework: Scott 1998 legibility; Brambor et al. 2020 information capacity
anchors: 0 local systems | 1 partial or local standard | 2 polity-wide standard measures or dating | 3 polity-wide measures and dating/calendar imposed
proxy: royal measures (gur of Akkade, gur lugal, mina of the king), dating systems (year names, regnal years, eponyms, era)
